To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the SRI method of rice cultivation has a potential to reduce pest incidence in rice and increase the economic returns of rice cultivation in India.
the SRI method of cultivation is beneficial to the environment and the farmers.
the application of organic nutrient sources in rice cultivation can be an alternative to inorganic fertilizers in terms of economics, pest management and soil health.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of organic nutrient sources on insect pests and economics of rice production in India.
the influence of different organic manures on insect pests and economics of rice cultivation under System of Rice Interventions (SRI) and conventional method of crop cultivation in India.
the development of a simple and cost-effective method for the control of rice pests.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the application of GM/GLM + organic sources (FYM or BGA or Azotobacter or PSB) or vermicomposting of FYM or neem cake would be a viable option for sustainable and environment friendly rice production in India.
the organic nutrient sources are more beneficial to the farmers in terms of economic returns and environmental safety than the inorganic fertilizers.

, the organic sources of nutrients viz., GM/GLM, neem cake and vermicompost are more beneficial than inorganic fertilizers for the management of insect pests and economics of irrigated rice production in India.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, the use of GM/GLM + Azotobacter + PSB as an organic nutrient source for rice production is more beneficial than the recommended dose of inorganic fertilizer.
the application of GM/GLM as organic nutrient source is a viable option to replace the recommended fertilizer dose in the rice production.
, organic nutrient sources can improve soil health and productivity of rice crop and can also help in improving the quality of rice.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the organic sources of nutrients can be used as a substitute to inorganic fertilizers in rice production.
the use of organic nutrient sources in combination with biofertilizers and bioagents in SRI cultivation is a promising approach for the production of healthy and quality rice.
the use of green leaf manure and green leaf manure + FYM + bio-fertilizers (PSB, BGA) in combination can improve the B: C ratio, and also increase the yield and benefit-cost ratio of rice.
